plan.title: Treated vs control muscle RNA-seq DE with outlier sensitivity
plan.analytical_narrative:
The dataset is a small unpaired bulk RNA-seq experiment: 12,000 gene-symbol rows x 11 columns in counts.csv (10 sample columns plus the gene-symbol column) and a 10-row metadata.csv carrying one condition column, 5 treated vs 5 control, single batch, Salmon gene-level raw counts, human skeletal muscle. The research question is simply which genes differ between treated and control, but the profile flags that sample_03 separates from every other sample on PCA and on the sample-distance heatmap. With n=5 per group, one aberrant sample can dominate dispersion estimation and either manufacture or erase hits, so the plan cannot just run DESeq2 once and report a list.

The plan therefore has three linked steps in one track. T1S1 formalises the QC verdict on sample_03 rather than inheriting it as an assertion: VST/rlog PCA with the fraction of variance on each PC, Euclidean sample-distance matrix, per-sample library size and detected-gene counts, per-sample median correlation to all others, and a Cook's-distance / relative-log-expression read on whether the separation looks like a technical outlier (low depth, low complexity, RLE offset) or like real within-group biology. Crucially it does not delete the sample; it records which group sample_03 belongs to and outputs a recommendation with the numbers behind it.

T1S2 runs the actual differential expression with DESeq2 on the raw integer counts, ~treated vs control with control as reference, twice: the full 5v5 design and the leave-one-out design without sample_03 (4 vs 5). Both are reported. The primary result is designated in advance — the full 10-sample fit — with the sensitivity fit used to label every gene as robust (significant in both) or outlier-dependent (significant in only one). This is the honest way to answer 'which genes differ' when one sample is suspect and the group size is 5: report the list and report how much of it survives removing the suspect sample, rather than silently picking whichever analysis gives more hits. Independent filtering, apeglm LFC shrinkage for ranking, and BH FDR are standard here; low-count prefiltering must use the same rule in both fits so the two gene universes are comparable.

T1S3 takes the shrunken ranking from the primary fit into gene-set enrichment against the staged human MSigDB hallmark and GO-BP collections (HGNC symbols, matching the gene-symbol row names). fgsea on the full ranked statistic is preferred over an over-representation test on a thresholded list, because a 5v5 design may yield few or no genes past FDR 0.05 and a ranked test still reports coordinated shifts. Enrichment is run on the primary ranking and repeated on the leave-one-out ranking so pathway-level conclusions carry the same robustness label as the gene-level ones.

The hard constraint throughout: this is n=5 per group, single batch, no covariates. No batch correction is warranted, no surrogate-variable modelling is justified with this sample size, and the write-up must state the power limit rather than dress a short hit list as a mechanism.
